summary: Weekly POC sync focused on follow-up from 4/20 reliability incident. Team triaged root causes (rate-limit throttling interactions with our proxy, occasional 5xx from model variants under burst), agreed on immediate mitigations (temporary rate increases, updated retry/backoff, turn on KV prefix caching for hot routes), and defined logs + benchmarks to validate fixes in staging before rolling to production pilot.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-22 15:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ethan Park (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Atlas CTO), Samir Patel (Lead ML Eng), Jorge Ramos (Infra Eng)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick agenda     quick agenda     incident recap, what we changed so far, and next steps. Samir, do you want to start with the timeline?
[00:18] Samir: Yeah sure, so on Monday, around 14:12 UTC we started seeing elevated p50/p95 on the inference route, and by 14:20 we saw a spike in 5xxs. Our proxy — sorry, our egress proxy started returning 502s back to callers. It looked like a mix of timeouts and the model backend occasionally returning 5xx when under burst.
[00:40] Jorge: to add, we had a hard limit set in our rate limiter, and when retries happened they amplified traffic which contributed to the backend queueing.
[00:55] Ethan: Right, that's pretty common — retry storms against a saturated model queue. We pulled the Redwood side traces and saw a sequence where requests hit the same shard and the KV cache miss rate was high for that prefix. So more compute per request and latency grew.
[01:15] Lena: Quick q — you said shard? are you suggesting the routing put them on the same worker?
[01:22] Ethan: We observed a routing concentration; it's more pronounced with short sequences hitting newer tokens. Could be due to the affinity policy in the pilot config.
[01:34] Maya: Ok, so root causes: proxy rate-limiter + retry amplification + routing concentration + higher backend cost due to KV cache misses. We pushed a quick mitigation this morning — increased per-route soft limit and tuned retries to exponential backoff with jitter.
[01:54] Samir: After the change we saw 60% reduction in 5xxs in staging, but production dropped only 30% — still seeing periodic timeouts.
[02:06] Ethan: Two follow-ups from SE: 1) We recommend turning on prefix KV caching for the hot routes (should cut cold-token compute). 2) Implement a client-side bounded retry with exponential backoff and capped attempts.
[02:23] Jorge: For prefix caching — will that be on Redwood or do we need to implement anything?
[02:29] Ethan: Redwood runtime supports prefix/KV caching on the serving side — it's a config flag in the route. We'll share the tuning docs. In your case I'd start with 2MB prefix cache per worker for the pilot.
[02:42] Maya: Also, we temporarily bumped the hosted rate for the pilot during the incident to keep availability, that was a manual override. We'll capture those changes in the audit log.
[02:53] Lena: We saw some mentions of 429s earlier — is that purely the proxy?
[02:58] Ethan: Mostly yes. The proxy returns 429 when limits hit. But combined with retries without backoff it becomes a heavier load.
[03:10] Samir: Quick note — we use a five second client timeout currently. Would you recommend increasing it?
[03:15] Ethan: I'd increase to 10s for critical routes, but better is to fix the underlying tail latency. Longer timeouts will hide problems and may exacerbate concurrency pressure.
[03:27] Maya: Let's walk through what we'll do before next sync. Ethan, can you enumerate the logs and artifacts you'll share?
[03:33] Ethan: Sure — per-route latency histograms, worker-level KV hit/miss stats, request traces around the 14:20 window, and our suggested retry/backoff snippets. I'll also include the serving runtime metrics (queue length, kernel load).
[03:45] Jorge: we'll also send our proxy logs and rate-limit config. there might be a small config mismatch — we had a stale rule.
[03:55] Lena: any security concerns with turning on prefix caching? we host some sensitive prompts.
[04:01] Ethan: Good question — the KV prefix cache is in-memory on the serving worker and not persisted. For extra safety you can enable customer-managed KMS to encrypt at rest for other components, but prefix cache stays in memory and is not written to disk. We can provide an architecture note.
[04:18] Maya: I'll send the security pack (SOC2 scope, KMS note, and audit log export example).
[04:24] Samir: On model side, could the variant we selected be less stable? We are on open-model-22b-fast.
[04:31] Ethan: We noticed that open-model-22b-fast has a higher tail latency under burst compared to the 22b-standard. We can test a fallback policy to route to 22b-standard for requests that cross a latency threshold; that'll reduce 5xxs at slight cost to latency and compute.
[04:48] Lena: What's the expected cost delta?
[04:51] Maya: We'll put numbers in the follow-up pricing note, but ballpark the standard variant is ~15% cheaper per token in your current profile.
[04:59] Samir: Another ask — can Redwood support a canary with traffic shaping? Like 10% to new variant while monitoring errors?
[05:06] Ethan: Yes, rollout policies support canary and automatic fallback based on error rate thresholds. We'll configure that for the benchmark run.
[05:15] Maya: okay, planning wise — we want logs by Friday (4/24) so we can validate, then run a throughput benchmark next week. Jorge, Samir, is that okay?
[05:24] Jorge: yes that's fine. we'll prioritize the proxy logs and the stale rule fix.
[05:29] Samir: We'll run the retry change in staging by Monday and report back.
[05:33] Lena: are there any alternate root causes we should keep an eye on? network glitches, cert rotation?
[05:39] Jorge: we had a cert rotation scheduled around that time but it completed before. we'll double-check. network-wise nothing in cloud provider status.
[05:48] Ethan: I'll also look for kernel timeouts in the runtime — occasionally a bad kernel selection under specific seq-len distributions causes transient 5xx.
[05:58] Maya: Great. let's capture the next steps.

Recap / Action items (verbatim):
[06:10] Maya: Ethan to share per-route latency logs, KV stats, serving runtime metrics, and retry config by 4/24.
[06:20] Maya: Maya to send security pack and updated pilot PRICING by 4/23.
[06:25] Samir: Atlas to apply retry/backoff in staging and report by 4/29.
[06:30] Jorge: Atlas to send proxy logs and validate rate-limit rule; testing cert rotation - due 4/28.

Questions noted:
- Should we temporarily increase timeouts? (consensus: increase slightly but fix tail latency)
- Is prefix KV cache safe for sensitive contexts? (answer: in-memory only, provide docs)

Shared links mentioned during call:
- Pilot benchmark spreadsheet (link)
- Redwood retry/backoff snippets (link)
- Security pack: SOC2 & KMS NOTE (link)

End of call.
